conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to check in on how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived.  
We’ll use a short, well-studied tool called the Edinburgh Postpartum/Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS). It’s simply ten questions about your mood, thoughts, and energy over the past seven days. Your answers stay confidential and help us figure out what extra support—if any—might make motherhood feel a little lighter.  
Whenever you’re ready, we’ll go through the questions one by one. There are no right or wrong answers; just whatever feels true for you today.

Let’s start:  
Over the past seven days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?

[sighs softly, gives a small shrug]  
I still laugh sometimes—like when my sister sent me a silly video—but it feels… flatter than it used to. I wouldn’t say it’s “difficult,” exactly, it just doesn’t bubble up the same way. Maybe three or four days this week I found myself smiling at little things, but it fades pretty fast.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Yeah… I’ve been able to laugh a little, but it’s not the same. It’s like the joy is kind of muted—like I have to remind myself to find things funny instead of just feeling it right away.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

[pauses, smoothing the blanket over my lap]  
I still look forward to some things—like my mom bringing dinner or the baby’s bath time—but the excitement is… dimmer. Most days I think “that’ll be nice,” rather than really feeling it.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Sometimes, yeah. Like yesterday the baby was fussy for hours and I caught myself thinking, “I must be doing something wrong—maybe he’s not getting enough milk because I didn’t nurse long enough.” I know it’s probably not true, but those thoughts still pop in. It’s not every minute, just once in a while.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Every now and then I’ll suddenly feel my heart race—like when the baby’s asleep I’ll tiptoe over to check if he’s still breathing. It’s not constant, maybe two or three times this week, and I can usually calm myself down by reminding myself he’s okay, but it still catches me off guard.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

I haven’t had full panic, but there was one night when I woke up suddenly and felt this wave of dread, like something bad was about to happen. My chest felt tight for a few minutes, and I couldn’t place why. It passed after I got up and drank some water, but it left me a little shaky.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yeah… a couple days this week it’s felt like the laundry and bottles and diaper changes just keep piling faster than I can finish them. I get a tight feeling in my chest, like I can’t quite catch my breath, but if I step away for a minute and breathe it settles. I’m still managing, just feels heavier than usual.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

No, it’s not that bad. I can fall asleep pretty easily once the baby settles. Sometimes it takes me a little longer if I’m running through the day in my head, but I wouldn’t say I’m so unhappy I can’t sleep.
I have felt sad or miserable

I do feel kind of sad some days—like a gray cloud sitting there—but it’s not overwhelming. It comes and goes. I’d say maybe three days this week I caught myself just feeling “blah” for stretches, but I can still smile at the baby when he coos.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

I’ve cried a couple of times—once when the baby wouldn’t latch and once when my partner asked how I was doing. It wasn’t all-day sobbing, just tears that came and went. I felt better after a shower and a nap.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—never. I haven’t had any thoughts like that.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 14: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Summary  
Date: [today]

Patient-reported symptoms (last 7 days):

<sym>Diminished pleasure / “muted joy”</sym> – laughs infrequently, anticipates events with only mild interest.  
<sym>Episodic low mood</sym> – “gray cloud,” present ~3 days; brief crying spells (×2) when feeding or questioned.  
<sym>Self-reproach</sym> – occasional unfounded guilt about infant care (feeding duration).  
<sym>Intermittent anxiety</sym> – nocturnal dread episode, brief tachycardia when infant sleeps; no full panic.  
<sym>Feeling overwhelmed</sym> – chores “heavier,” chest tightness, resolves with brief break.  
Sleep initiation mildly delayed by rumination; no persistent insomnia.  
No self-harm ideation.

Pattern: Mild-to-moderate anhedonia and labile mood, situational anxiety, intact reality testing, no safety concerns.

Risk flags: Subjective joy reduction, episodic tearfulness, transient anxiety/physiological arousal, coping strain.  
Screening consideration: Meets partial criteria for minor/major postpartum depression and/or postpartum anxiety; further evaluation recommended.

End of screening note
